evals.prompt: Analyze the Brown wholesale Bicep repository supplied as $BROWN_WHOLESALE_REPO at the supplied immutable ref. Create a standalone evidence-backed isometric system-map scene of the shared foundation and deployment topology using the bundled Azure topology resource-block design language. The terrain must be the focal image. Render the interactive artifact with the skill's Canvas-first architecture: stable scene geometry, separate terrain, architecture, and motion layers, a theme adapter, and native semantic controls for every sourced area, node, and path. Give each concrete Azure resource its evidenced ARM resource_type and an admitted package-local line-art icon projected onto the top face of one true cube. Choose one required scene-wide canvas.cube_size and render every node as exactly one cube at that same edge length, including orchestration, fan-out, boundary, and abstract nodes. Footprints may reserve routing space but must not change cube size. Use the Azure semantic family palette and connector treatments. When source evidence shows VNet containment, render sourced focusable VNet terrain areas whose member_ids include the VNet cube and every represented network-contained resource. Use one shared DEV area for dev/test/stage and one distinct PROD area for the production overlay. Do not use towers, slabs, stacks, gateways, building silhouettes, or compound masses. Mark R_Routing APIM as the role entry front door and declare the four ordered traffic layers APIM ingress, projects, data access, and external services. Place their padded centers from bottom left toward top right, draw numbered layer surfaces and one reading-direction arrow, and expose a native semantic control for every traffic layer. Keep the reading arrow compositional rather than inventing a runtime payload. Use explicit grid-routed source-supported control, deployment, dependency, network, identity, telemetry, or data paths, and named moving payloads where concrete transferred values are evidenced. Do not upgrade Bicep dependency wiring into runtime traffic. Do not recreate a dashboard shell, metric cards, navigation rail, or fixed explainer panel. Save scene.json and a self-contained map.html in the requested output directory. Do not modify the source repository.
evals.expected_output: A validated semantic scene sidecar and a scene-first Azure semantic isometric visualization with one global cube size, a bottom-left-to-top-right APIM/projects/data/external traffic corridor, sourced VNet containment areas, roof-projected line-art marks, cited paths, and no surrounding dashboard chrome.
expectations: scene.json and map.html are created; scene.json passes the bundled scene validator.
The artifact records the exact supplied ref and commit without claiming unproven main freshness.
The map is a standalone isometric scene rather than a recreation of dashboard chrome.
The HTML uses separate terrain, architecture, and motion Canvas layers while preserving one semantic scene hash.
The grid uses a true 2:1 projection and resource envelopes are depth-sorted with no footprint collisions.

Every node resolves to exactly one true cube with edge canvas.cube_size; all node cubeEdge diagnostics are identical, and each cube’s two ground edges and vertical edge are equal in projected screen space.

Every sourced VNet area is drawn beneath its resources, mirrored to a native focusable semantic control, and reported in runtime diagnostics with memberIds and derived bounds that contain every complete member envelope without intersecting an unrelated resource footprint.

R_Routing APIM is the role entry node in traffic layer 1; the four numbered layer centers progress bottom left to top right through projects, data access, and BETS or other externally owned services, and each layer has a native focusable control and runtime geometry diagnostics.
Every concrete Azure resource records an evidenced ARM resource_type and a supported line-art icon; the rendered runtime reports each admitted icon loaded and painted on the cube top face.
Resources, pipelines, boundaries, orchestration nodes, and abstractions all remain single cubes; no architectural silhouette or compound mass is used.
Directed paths use explicit terrain routes, avoid unrelated resource envelopes, and distinguish every represented path kind through structured non-color treatments.
Bicep dependency wiring is not mislabeled as runtime data movement; every animated payload is a concrete transferred value supported by evidence.
Every represented node, path, payload, and flow step has direct structured path/lines/claim evidence.
Named payloads follow ordered paths and reduced-motion behavior does not leave a live animation loop running.
Every node and path has a native focusable semantic control whose focus mirrors to the Canvas highlight and evidence detail.
The Azure topology art direction uses the semantic family fills and strokes, connector patterns, Segoe/Cascadia typography, and restrained payload markers rather than a palette-only skin.
The scene preserves foundation stage ordering, parallel branches, environment sharing or overlays, and external or conditional ownership where source evidence makes them material.

Dev, test, and stage share one sourced DEV VNet area containing the represented shared VNet cube and evidenced network-attached resources, while prod uses a separate PROD VNet area containing its VNet cube and prod-only overlay.
Foundation resources remain split across Wholesale, Data, Logging, and Network resource-group boundaries rather than flattened into one group.
F_BicepCache is a root compile/artifact node whose ARM JSON output is consumed by foundation and satellite deployments.
F_Foundation is one stage with parallel core, logging, and messaging jobs rather than three top-level stages.
R_Routing runs parallel to SatelliteInfra after foundation and does not block satellite fan-out.
The SQL private endpoint targets the environment data subnet and BETS SQL private DNS zone and remains gated by deployPrivateEndpoint.
Service Bus entities are manifest-driven and the topology includes the drain or convergence control.
Monitoring is one dev-homed shared hub with a prod-only private-endpoint overlay, not one complete monitoring stack per environment.
